extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Agencies; agency standards executives; regulatory and procurement officials; agency ethics officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agencies on using and participating in voluntary consensus standards bodies and on reporting and managing standards use and conformity assessment activities under OMB Circular A-119 (Revised).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal participation must be in the public interest and compatible with agency missions
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal participation in the development of technical standards is appropriate “when such participation is in the public interest and is compatible with agency and departmental missions, authorities, and budget resources.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative history indicates the Act intended to promote federal participation; agencies should ensure participation furthers mission and fits within authorities and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote full and equal federal participation in voluntary consensus standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act was intended to promote full and equal participation in voluntary consensus standards bodies by federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither the Act nor its history indicates federal representatives are to have less than full and equal representation; agencies should support full participation consistent with policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not direct internal operations of private SDOs
rubrics_metrics.description: It is inappropriate for the federal government to direct the internal operations of private sector voluntary consensus standards bodies or standards development organizations (SDOs) by proscribing the activities of any of its members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not attempt to dictate SDO governance (choice of chair, voting procedures, funding). Expect SDOs or accrediting organizations to ensure fairness and balanced proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit agency support to that which clearly furthers agency missions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 7 expressly limits agency support (e.g., funding, participation, etc.) to “that which clearly furthers agency and departmental missions, authorities, priorities, and budget resources.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency has no mission-related or statutory purpose in participation, then participation would be contrary to the Circular; agencies must justify support as mission-furthering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies are responsible to avoid inconsistent participation and perceptions of impropriety
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency is ultimately responsible for ensuring that its members are not participating in voluntary consensus standards bodies in a manner inconsistent with the Circular and the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should monitor participation to prevent dominating proceedings or creating an appearance of impropriety; involve ethics officers and follow agency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with private-sector oversight organizations to prevent abuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should work closely with private sector oversight organizations to ensure that no abuses occur in standards development activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments from ANSI describe oversight mechanisms; agencies are encouraged to cooperate with and support private-sector oversight to maintain fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between technical standards and regulatory standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular distinguishes a “technical standard,” which may be referenced in a regulation, from a “regulatory standard,” which establishes overall regulatory goals or outcomes; the Act and Circular apply to the former, not the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical standards pertain to products and processes (size, strength, technical performance) and may be incorporated into regulation; agencies are not required to use private-sector standards that would set regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourage reliance on government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of the Circular is to discourage the government's reliance on government-unique standards and to encourage agencies to rely on voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular does not create discrimination among private-sector standards (consensus, industry, company or de facto); agencies should prefer voluntary consensus standards unless inconsistent with law or impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency use of standards is determined agency-by-agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of the Circular’s policies is on an agency-by-agency and case-by-case basis; use of a voluntary consensus standard by one agency does not require another agency to use the same standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may have different needs and may decide a voluntary consensus standard is contrary to law or otherwise impractical for their program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may use government-unique standards when inconsistent with law or impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may choose their own government-unique standard “where inconsistent with applicable law or otherwise impractical.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular and Act already state this exception; untimeliness or unavailability of voluntary consensus standards may be reasonable justification; agencies should document rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure standards chosen are true consensus standards and provide public reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular expands the definition of “consensus” and describes how agencies may identify voluntary consensus standards and establishes reporting procedures that allow for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow final section 4a(1)(v) and section 6l for identifying standards and use reporting procedures to enable public input on decisions to use or not use voluntary consensus standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider international voluntary consensus standards where possible but do not mandate preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular states that standards developed by international voluntary consensus standards bodies “should be considered in procurement and regulatory applications” but does not mandate preference or preempt treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider international as well as domestic voluntary consensus standards when feasible; the Circular does not create discrimination between international and domestic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give preference to performance-based standards when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: “Preference should be given to standards based on performance criteria.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performance standards can be used in lieu of other types of standards (e.g., safety or health regulations), agencies should prefer performance-based criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect copyright holders when standards are referenced in regulation (balanced approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Language regarding protection of copyright holders when standards are referenced in regulation was considered and the Circular’s chosen wording was retained as appropriately balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow the Circular’s guidance (final sections 6k, 7j) to address copyright concerns while enabling use of standards in regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should identify sources for voluntary consensus standards (NIST, agencies, publishers)
rubrics_metrics.description: This section provides guidance on where agencies may go to identify voluntary consensus standards; in addition to NIST, standards may be identified through other federal agencies and standards publishing companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should use NIST plus other federal sources and standards publishers as applicable to identify voluntary consensus standards for procurement and regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies are not required to publish individual Federal Register notices for each federal participant
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring Federal Register notices whenever a federal employee is to participate in a voluntary consensus standards body would be overly burdensome; instead agencies must publish a directory of federal participants in standards organizations (section 15b(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should maintain and publish the required directory rather than issuing notices per participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal participants must be authorized and act at government expense when representing agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal employees who are representing their agency must do so at federal expense and must be specifically authorized agency representatives; employees may maintain personal memberships in outside organizations unless agency requires prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation at higher leadership levels (officers, directors) requires additional scrutiny; employees should consult agency ethics officers for applicable restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit participation only when compatible with missions, authorities, priorities, and budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency participation is permitted when it is compatible with agency and departmental missions, authorities, priorities, and budget resources, consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must apply this compatibility test when deciding to support or authorize participation in standards bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid practice or appearance of undue influence by agency employees in SDOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency employees, whether or not in a position of leadership in a voluntary consensus standards body, must avoid the practice or appearance of undue influence relating to the agency’s representation and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final section 7g modified to clarify avoidance of undue influence; involve agency ethics officers prior to authorizing support or participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep number of individual agency participants to a minimum (guidance not mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular retains language that keeping the number of individual agency participants to a minimum is a recommendation (“should” rather than “shall”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are advised to limit participants but the Circular does not make this an absolute mandatory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No general requirement to disclose amount of federal support to public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular declines to require that the amount of federal support be made public or provided to the supported committee because it is expected to be known to the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are not required to publish the amount of federal support, though oversight and transparency are encouraged via other mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards activities ordinarily not subject to FACA but agencies should be aware of FACA issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal participation in standards activities would not ordinarily be subject to the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) because private sector members are developing standards rather than advising the government; nevertheless agencies should be aware of potential FACA issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must assess circumstances where FACA might apply and take appropriate steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage balanced revisions that promote participation but discourage dominance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular’s revisions are balanced to encourage agency participation while also discouraging agency dominance of SDOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative history supports more full federal participation while the Circular includes safeguards to prevent dominance and ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a process for ongoing review of agencies' use of standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are responsible for “establishing a process for ongoing review of the agency’s use of standards for purposes of updating such use.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces a fixed five-year review; agencies are encouraged to review uses of obsolete or government-unique standards as soon as practicable and to update regulations referencing outdated standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to automatically accept requests from VCS bodies to replace federal standards outside review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are not required to respond to requests from voluntary consensus standards bodies to replace existing federal standards, specifications, or regulations beyond the established review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular’s review process (per comment 59) suffices; agencies should use their established procedures to consider such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPRM/final rule must provide notice about standards use but not an extensive report
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must provide analysis of the use and non-use of voluntary consensus standards in NPRMs and final rules to enable public comment, but are not expected to provide an extensive report with each rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NPRMs, agencies may include a few sentences identifying the proposed standard and, if applicable, a simple explanation why a government-unique standard is proposed instead of a voluntary consensus standard. Most rulemakings will not reference standards and thus require no statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No need for a separate 'sufficiency of agency search' section
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB decided a separate section on 'Sufficiency of Agency Search' to limit agency obligation to search for existing voluntary consensus standards is unnecessary given other Circular requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should rely on the identification procedures elsewhere in the Circular rather than a separate sufficiency-test provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies are not required to conduct their own scientific review of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular declines to require agencies to fully investigate and review the scientific intent and capabilities of a voluntary consensus standard because SDOs adhere to lengthy procedures that scrutinize uses and capabilities of standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adopting a standard for procurement or regulation, agencies remain required to undertake applicable reviews under the Act, the Circular, Federal Acquisition Regulation, Executive Order 12866, and other relevant sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Standards Executives and ICSP advise on compliance; OMB oversight limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Standards Executives, with advice of the Chair of the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy (ICSP), are responsible for ensuring agencies comply with the Circular; OMB did not take on more defined oversight responsibility in this revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect SDOs to help ensure compliance and work with Standards Executives where necessary; minor clarifying language inserted in sections 13–15.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIST coordinates public-sector standards and conformity assessment activities while affirming ANSI role
rubrics_metrics.description: NIST is to “coordinate Federal, State, and local technical standards activities and conformity assessment activities with private sector ... activities.” This coordination is of the public sector; ANSI’s private-sector role is affirmed in an MOU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST’s role does not supplant ANSI; agencies should follow NIST guidance and respect ANSI’s representation of U.S. interests per the MOU.
